chunk_findings.detail: The new unquoted alternative `a/[^\s"]+`/`b/[^\s"]+` cannot match a real `git diff` header whose filename contains a space. `git diff` emits this as unquoted: `diff --git a/foo bar b/foo bar` for a file named `foo bar`. `_FILE.match` returns `None` for that line, so `shape` never appends `foo bar` to `self.files`. A patch whose first file has a space causes all of that file's lines to be skipped while `self.files` is empty, so the too-many-files bound sees fewer files than the patch contains and can be bypassed by under-count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: A filename containing a double quote is emitted by Git with the quote C-escaped inside a quoted side, e.g. `diff --git "a/foo\"bar" "b/foo\"bar"` for the path `foo"bar`. The quoted alternatives `"a/[^"]*"` and `"b/[^"]*"` stop at that escaped quote byte (`\"` is a literal `"` character in the patch text), so the regex cannot consume the closing quote and `_FILE.match` returns `None`. `_dequote` has a `"` escape specifically to decode `\"`, but the regex never lets such a path reach it; the file is omitted from `self.files`, under-counting the patch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `not q.malformed` for a patch containing two distinct file paths. That is inverted: this is the exact case where the too-many-files bound the test claims to guard should mark the patch malformed. With the fixed `_dequote`, `q.files` has length 2, so `P.shape(patch).malformed` is True and the assertion fails. The correct expectation is `assert q.malformed`; collapse of `\200`/`\201` to a single `U+FFFD` would incorrectly produce `not q.malformed`, which is the under-count being prevented.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_handoff_events.py:test_distinct_quoted_non_utf8_names_stay_distinct

chunk_findings.detail: `_FILE` only accepts an unquoted side with no whitespace or `"`, or a quoted side with no raw `"` at all. Git’s default `core.quotePath` emits a name containing `"` as `diff --git "a/foo\"bar" "b/foo\"bar"`; `"[^"]*"` stops at the escaped quote, `$` fails, and the header is ignored. `shape` then never appends that path, and because `not self.files` skips later hunks the patch is recorded as zero files and not malformed — so a suggestion of many such files stays under the too-many-files bound (fail-open). The same miss hits `core.quotePath=false` plus a space: `diff --git a/my file.txt b/my file.txt` does not match `[^\s"]+`, so that file is dropped even though the new comment says unquoted names must be counted as literal paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11

chunk_findings.detail: The new unquoted-side grammar `a/[^\s"]+(?:\s+[^\s"]+)*`/`b/[^\s"]+(?:\s+[^\s"]+)*` still rejects valid `core.quotePath=false` Git headers whose POSIX name begins with whitespace or contains a raw `"`. For example, `git -c core.quotePath=false diff` for a tracked file named ` foo` emits `diff --git a/ foo b/ foo`; `_FILE.match()` returns `None`, so `shape` never enters the header branch and never appends ` foo`. While `self.files` is empty, the `elif not self.files or self.in_binary: pass` branch then skips that file's remaining lines. A patch containing many such files is counted as zero files and is not marked malformed, bypassing the too-many-files bound instead of failing closed. The code comment at the `b = ...` line claims an unquoted name is a literal POSIX byte string, but this grammar does not accept all literal POSIX byte strings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11

chunk_findings.detail: The test treats `\303\251` as the raw `quotePath=false` output for `é`, but that is actually Git's C-quoted octal escape, not raw output. With `core.quotePath=false`, Git emits the raw UTF-8 bytes for `é`, which in a Python `str` is the character `\u00e9` (or surrogateescaped bytes `\udcc3\udca9` when decoded from raw bytes), not the ASCII characters backslash+digits. So an input like `diff --git a/é b/é` would be the real raw-byte case, and a bug that mangles raw unquoted non-ASCII names would still pass this test; the new test is missing/vacuous for the behavior it claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_handoff_events.py:test_unquoted_name_is_a_literal_byte_string

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten matcher still misparses valid Git diff headers when a path contains the literal sequence ` b/` because the lazy `(?P<a>.+?)` and `(?P<b>.+?)` make the first ` b/` after `a/` play the role of the separator. For a file named `foo" b/bar`, Git emits `diff --git "a/foo\" b/bar" "b/foo\" b/bar"`; `_FILE.match` stops at the first interior ` b/`, so `m["b"]` is `bar" "b/foo\" b/bar"`, not `foo" b/bar`. `shape.files` therefore records the wrong filename, breaking file tracking and file-count distinctness for a legitimate patch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: The change still does not answer the previous review’s “assert q.malformed” expectation. This test builds a patch with two `diff --git` headers, and the adjacent `over` fixture asserts that a two-file patch is `malformed`, but this test now only checks `q.files == ("\udc80", "\udc81")`. The erroneous `not q.malformed` was removed, but the correct too-many-files assertion was not added: a regression that kept the two non-UTF-8 names distinct yet failed to set `malformed` for the two-file patch would pass this test, leaving the exact too-many-files guard still unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_handoff_events.py:test_distinct_quoted_non_utf8_names_stay_distinct

chunk_findings.detail: `_FILE` uses non-greedy matching `(?P<a>.+?)` and `(?P<b>.+?)` anchored by `(?P=aq)` and `(?P=bq)`. Given a quoted patch line where the filename contains spaces or is followed by other text inside the quotes, or when `git diff` produces standard quoted paths with spaces such as `diff --git "a/foo bar" "b/foo bar"`, `(?P<a>.+?)` will match the shortest possible string before any space if a space appears inside the quoted path, or it will fail to match correctly because `.+?` stops at the first space when unquoted or interacts wrongly with quotes. Specifically, for an unquoted path containing a space (e.g., `diff --git a/foo bar b/foo bar`), `(?P<a>.+?)` matches `foo`, leaving `bar` unconsumed before `b/`, causing `_FILE.match` to return `None`. Thus, handoff patch parsing completely drops valid git diff headers for filenames with spaces when `core.quotePath` is false or when paths are unquoted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11

chunk_findings.detail: The unquoted alternative splits on the first ` b/` rather than the real a/b separator. Given the real `core.quotePath` header `diff --git a/a b/c.txt b/a b/c.txt` (directory `a b`, file `c.txt`; a plain space is not quoted), `(?P<a>.+?)` stops at the space inside the a-path, so `m["b"]` is `c.txt b/a b/c.txt` and `shape` records that instead of `a b/c.txt`. The same false split hits any unquoted path containing the substring ` b/` (a directory name ending in ` b`), so the new space-handling path keeps the wrong identity even though the header matched.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: The previous unquoted-path misparse still holds. With `core.quotePath=false`, a file named `a b/c.txt` produces Git header `diff --git a/a b/c.txt b/a b/c.txt`. In `(?P<a>"a/(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"|a/.*) `, the greedy `a/.*` backtracks to the last space that still lets the `b` group start with `b/`, which here is the space inside the b-side name. `m["b"]` therefore becomes `b/c.txt`, so `shape` records `"c.txt"` instead of `"a b/c.txt"`. This is valid Git output, not malformed, so file tracking silently uses the wrong filename.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: The patch built in this test contains two `diff --git` headers (for `\200` and `\201`). The same test suite already establishes that a two-`diff --git` input must be `malformed`: `test_quoted_paths_overstated_headers_and_countered_resets` asserts `P.shape(over).malformed` for a two-file patch. This test only asserts `q.files == ("\udc80", "\udc81")`, so a regression that returns the two distinct decoded names yet fails to set `malformed` for this two-file patch would pass unnoticed. The missing too-many-files assertion is still not added.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_handoff_events.py:test_distinct_quoted_non_utf8_names_stay_distinct

chunk_findings.detail: The new matcher still records the wrong name for an unquoted path that contains the substring ` b/`. `a/.*` is greedy, so the engine backtracks to the rightmost split whose remainder matches `b/.*`. Given quotePath=false input `diff --git a/foo b/bar b/foo b/bar` (directory `foo b`, file `bar`), that split is the space inside the b-path, so `m["b"]` is `b/bar` and `shape.files` is `("bar",)` rather than `("foo b/bar",)`. The quoted-path tests do not cover this header, and `test_unquoted_name_with_space_is_literal` only uses a name where ` b/` occurs once, so it passes while this input does not. The previous unquoted-separator finding is therefore still open; the failure mode moved from the first ` b/` to the last.
